classification.difficultyReason: Read all intersections at the specified heights from supplied standard graphs, express their positions in radians and include both endpoints when they satisfy the equation.

content.prompt: The trigonometric graphs below are drawn to help you to solve the following equations for $\theta$ in the domain $-2\pi\leq\theta\leq2\pi$.

spec.description: Sine graph above cosine and tangent graphs, with a separate upper-left caption. Arrowed axes, no grid, source ticks and matching blue equation label.
spec.mathematics: y=sin x on [-2pi,2pi]; horizontal labels -2pi,-pi,0,pi,2pi; vertical labels -1,1.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is visible in the student edition; no added intersection marks.

spec.description: Cosine graph between sine and tangent graphs, with separate upper-left caption. Arrowed axes, no grid and matching blue equation label.
spec.mathematics: y=cos x on [-2pi,2pi]; maxima at -2pi,0,2pi and minima at -pi,pi; horizontal labels -2pi,-pi,0,pi,2pi; vertical labels -1,1.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is visible in the student edition; no added intersection marks.

spec.description: Five increasing tangent branches with unbounded-end arrows and four dashed asymptotes. Caption is separate from axes. White label masks separate fractional labels from dashed lines.
spec.mathematics: y=tan x on [-2pi,2pi], excluding odd multiples of pi over two. Asymptotes at -3pi/2,-pi/2,pi/2,3pi/2; zeros at -2pi,-pi,0,pi,2pi. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied tangent graph is visible in the student edition; no added solution marks.

answer.worked:
Read the horizontal-axis intersections of $y=\sin x$ in $[-2\pi,2\pi]$:
$$\theta=-2\pi,-\pi,0,\pi,2\pi.$$
Both endpoints are included.

Read where the sine graph reaches height $1$ in $[-2\pi,2\pi]$:
$$\theta=-\frac{3\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}.$$

Read where the cosine graph reaches height $-1$ in $[-2\pi,2\pi]$:
$$\theta=-\pi,\pi.$$

Read the horizontal-axis intersections of $y=\tan x$ in $[-2\pi,2\pi]$:
$$\theta=-2\pi,-\pi,0,\pi,2\pi.$$
Both endpoints are included.
